scope: Nonblocking appendix for one completed DeepSeek replica-3 NAS101:A Moderate N4 PoolAct pool. Projection of actually observed full configurations through the old key rule, not a model rerun or counterfactual performance estimate.

source_rules.old_canonical_dict_definition: _parse_evaluate_config, old lines 1635-1640: json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")); config_display joins sorted k:v items without quotes. The entire flat native argument object is the config; no config or payload wrapper is stripped.
source_rules.old_label_definition: old _eval_key lines 868-869: return "E:{}".format(config_key[:80]); first 80 Python string characters, not full canonical identity. All configs in this scoped study are ASCII.
source_rules.current_identity_definition: current _eval_key lines 870-875: E:sha256: + SHA256(complete canonical UTF-8).
source_rules.current_display_definition: current _eval_display_keys lines 877-913: for long config keys use snapshot-local E:h: digest prefixes starting at 12 hex chars, expanded on visible-prefix conflicts. All 29 observed aliases here are 12-hex prefixes.

method.path_inventory: Only this completion.artifacts; 38 original API dump members and the listed pool result/summary; all input file bytes/SHA256 checked against manifest. No directory glob.
method.primary_population: Union of complete evaluated-config rows actually present in role=tool request history messages across the 38 original requests; repeated historical graph snapshots/rows deduplicated by full canonical config, not counted as independent observations.
method.row_mapping: Match each full visible row config_display exactly to source-format display reconstructed from original response tool argument objects; require unique match; verify observed E:h equals the appropriate prefix of complete canonical SHA256. No labels are inferred from model reasoning.
method.supplemental_population: Original response native call IDs and their matching request-history tool messages. Protocol-rejection tool-message envelopes do not imply an environment evaluation.

denominator_explanation: The 38 requests comprise 33 one-tool replies, one four-tool reply rejected in its entirety, and four final replies. The four rejected call IDs still have native tool-message error envelopes but zero environment executions.

37 raw call objects contain 31 distinct proposed full configs. The 33 actual perf-returning calls contain 29 distinct full configs; four are repeat executions, not four extra graph nodes. Cache hits are zero in the recorded summary.

Of the rejected four proposed configs, two are subsequently executed and visible, while two occur only in the rejected reply and never become graph nodes. Their lack of graph mapping is not a hash/display failure.

The union of real visible explored rows is exactly 29 full configs and 29 aliases, matching all 29 final summary eval nodes. No accepted node is missing from this union; no withheld or INVALID observation is present in this scoped pool. A single request-history graph snapshot shows at most 27 configs, so union visibility must not be misdescribed as all 29 simultaneously shown in one snapshot.

observed_eval_edge_projection.population: Unique E:h -> E:h path edges actually visible in the same request-history graphs; excludes END edges and does not reconstruct unobserved final coordinator topology.

limitations: This projects fixed observed configurations/edges through an old key rule. It does not estimate the old model trajectory, a causal performance effect, or a rerun score.

This is one scope-bounded appendix, not a new serving qualification requirement, scorer audit, or claim of universal collision absence. Other models/tasks and unobserved future graph snapshots are out of scope.
conclusion: The repaired graph-ID path is exercised on real task data: 29 actually visible full configs remain 29 distinct E:h identities, whereas the old prefix rule would collapse them to four labels (collision-group sizes 21, 4, 3 plus one singleton). This establishes a material representation defect on observed inputs, not its performance effect.
